Sliding-Window K-NN or PCA Imputation

Source: R/slide_imp.R
slide_imp.Rd

Impute missing values in a numeric matrix whose columns are ordered by position, using K-NN or PCA imputation within sliding windows. For Illumina DNA methylation microarrays, use group_imp() instead.

Usage

slide_imp(
  obj,
  location,
  window_size,
  overlap_size = 0,
  flank = FALSE,
  min_window_n,
  subset = NULL,
  dry_run = FALSE,
  k = NULL,
  cores = 1,
  dist_pow = 0,
  ncp = NULL,
  scale = TRUE,
  coeff.ridge = 1,
  threshold = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  row.w = NULL,
  nb.init = 1,
  maxiter = 1000,
  miniter = 5,
  solver = c("auto", "exact", "lobpcg"),
  lobpcg_control = NULL,
  clamp = NULL,
  method = NULL,
  .progress = TRUE,
  colmax = 0.9,
  post_imp = TRUE,
  on_infeasible = c("skip", "error", "mean")
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix. Samples are in rows and features in columns.

location

Numeric. The position of each column of obj, such as a genomic coordinate, sorted in ascending order.

window_size

Numeric. The width of each window, in the units of location. With flank = TRUE, the distance each window reaches on each side of its feature.

overlap_size

Numeric. The overlap between consecutive windows, in the units of location, less than window_size. Ignored when flank = TRUE.

flank

Logical. If FALSE, slide windows across all columns. If TRUE, build one window around each column in subset, as described under Details.

min_window_n

Integer. The smallest number of columns, at least 2, that a window needs to be kept. k and ncp must be less than min_window_n.

subset

Optional character or integer vector. The columns to impute and return, by name or by number, or NULL for every column. Must be supplied when flank = TRUE. Defaults to NULL.

dry_run

Logical. If TRUE, return the windows that min_window_n and subset leave, as a slideimp_tbl, without imputing. k and ncp are not needed then.

k

Integer or NULL. Number of nearest neighbors for K-NN imputation.

cores

Integer. Number of cores for K-NN imputation. Defaults to 1.

dist_pow

Numeric. Power used to penalize more distant neighbors in the weighted average, where 0 gives an unweighted average. The weighting rule is given under Details in knn_imp().

ncp

Integer or NULL. Number of components for PCA imputation.

scale

Logical. If TRUE, columns are scaled to unit variance.

coeff.ridge

Numeric. The ridge regularization for method = "regularized", ignored otherwise. Values below 1 move toward EM PCA, and values above 1 move toward mean imputation.

threshold

Numeric. Convergence threshold.

seed

Integer, numeric, or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. As in missMDA::imputePCA(), initialization i is seeded with seed * (i - 1). So seed = 0 gives every random initialization the same start, and nb.init then yields two distinct solves: the mean initialization and one random one. With nb.init > 1, seed can be at most .Machine$integer.max %/% (nb.init - 1).

row.w

Numeric vector, "n_miss", or NULL. The row weights, normalized to sum to 1: positive values of length nrow(obj), "n_miss" to down-weight rows with more missing values, or NULL for equal weights.

nb.init

Integer. Number of initializations. The first is always mean imputation, and the others are random.

maxiter

Integer. Maximum number of iterations.

miniter

Integer. Minimum number of iterations, at most maxiter.

solver

Character. One of "auto", "exact", or "lobpcg". The eigensolver. "auto" uses "exact" for small problems and otherwise runs a short timed probe, picking "lobpcg" only when it is clearly faster. With nb.init > 1, the choice from the first initialization is reused. See the PCA Performance tips section.

lobpcg_control

A list or NULL. LOBPCG control options, from lobpcg_control() or as a plain named list, or NULL for the defaults. Ignored when solver = "exact".

clamp

Numeric vector of length 2 or NULL. The bounds c(lower, upper) for PCA-imputed values, such as c(0, 1) for DNA methylation beta values, or NULL for none. Use -Inf or Inf for a one-sided bound. Observed values are not clamped.

method

Character or NULL. One of "euclidean" or "manhattan" for K-NN imputation, or "regularized" or "EM" for PCA imputation. NULL uses "euclidean" for K-NN and "regularized" for PCA.

.progress

Logical. If TRUE, show imputation progress.

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Columns with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax take no part in the imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

post_imp

Logical. If TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

on_infeasible

Character. One of "skip", "error", or "mean". The action for a window that is infeasible for imputation, for example because k or ncp is too large for the columns that colmax leaves. Defaults to "skip".

Value

If dry_run = FALSE, a numeric matrix of class slideimp_results with the rows of obj and the columns that subset selects, with missing values imputed.

If dry_run = TRUE, a data frame of class slideimp_tbl with one row per window and the columns start and end (the first and last column of obj in the window), window_n, subset_local and, when flank = TRUE, target.

Details

slide_imp() splits the columns of obj into windows by location and imputes each window on its own. There are two windowing modes:

  • flank = FALSE: greedily partition location into windows of width window_size with the requested overlap_size between consecutive windows. A window that would add no column to the window before it is not created. A column in more than one window takes the mean of their imputed values.

  • flank = TRUE: create one window per feature in subset. Each window covers the location values within window_size of that feature, on both sides, so it spans twice window_size.

Supply exactly one of k and ncp. k imputes each window with knn_imp(), and ncp imputes it with pca_imp(). The arguments of the other method are ignored.

The result holds the subset columns in the order they have in obj. In each window, every column the method can use takes part in the imputation, in subset or not: for K-NN every column within colmax, and for PCA every column within colmax whose variance is not zero. A name that is not in colnames(obj), or a subset that selects no column, is an error.

on_infeasible = "skip" does not impute an infeasible window, "mean" fills it with column means, and "error" stops at the first such window. With "skip" and "mean", slide_imp() raises one warning of class slideimp_fallback that lists the affected windows.

An infeasible window adds nothing to the mean_filled_cols and mean_filled_cells attributes. Where windows overlap, mean_filled_cells lists each cell that at least one window filled with its column mean.

With solver = "auto", the first window that completes the solver probe picks the solver, and every later window uses it.

slide_imp() rejects a column with no observed values only when a window covers it. A column that no window covers is returned unchanged.

Column mean fill

A column with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax takes no part in the imputation. The method neither uses the column to impute other columns nor imputes it.

With post_imp = TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after the method has run. Two kinds of missing value can remain: the missing values of the columns that took no part, and the cells for which the method found no value. Each column mean is the mean of the column's observed values. With post_imp = FALSE, both kinds stay missing.

The result records what the column means replaced, in two attributes:

  • mean_filled_cols: an integer vector with the index, in the result, of each column that took no part and was filled.

  • mean_filled_cells: an integer matrix with the columns row and col, one row for each cell that the method could not impute and that was filled.

Both attributes are empty when no column mean was used. print() reports them when they are not empty.

Missing values and non-finite input

obj must be a double matrix. An integer or logical matrix is rejected, not converted. Convert one with storage.mode(obj) <- "double".

NA and NaN are both treated as missing. The package does not distinguish between them.

Inf and -Inf are rejected on entry, and so is a column with no observed values (every cell NA or NaN). Locate them with which(is.infinite(obj), arr.ind = TRUE) and which(colSums(!is.na(obj)) == 0).

PCA Performance tips

Three arguments set the speed: solver, threshold, and scale. Tune these first, then the accuracy arguments ncp and coeff.ridge, on a representative subset.

Exact vs. LOBPCG. "lobpcg" suits large, approximately low-rank matrices with small ncp. "exact" suits small matrices, such as slide_imp() windows, where it is faster. It is also more reliable: it always converges, to eigenvectors exact to machine precision, while LOBPCG stops at the tolerance set in lobpcg_control() and can take many iterations, or reach maxiter, when the eigenvalues around the ncp-th one are close together. The warm start makes each later LOBPCG solve cheap: pca_imp() starts LOBPCG from the previous eigenblock and search direction, so once the imputed values stabilize, each solve takes a few iterations. The gain grows with the number of EM iterations, whatever the rank. solver = "auto", the default, chooses between the two and is a safe start.

Threshold. The default 1e-6 is conservative. 1e-5 is often faster and gives very similar values.

Scale. For columns on a common scale, such as DNA methylation beta values in [0, 1], scale = FALSE can be faster and more accurate.

BLAS. On Windows, the BLAS that ships with R can be slow, and OpenBLAS can replace it.

See Speeding up PCA imputation for the full workflow.

Examples

set.seed(1234)

# Example data with 20 samples and 100 ordered columns
beta_matrix <- sim_mat(20, 100)$input
location <- 1:100

# First perform a dry run to inspect the calculated windows
window_statistics <- slide_imp(
  beta_matrix,
  location = location,
  window_size = 50,
  overlap_size = 10,
  min_window_n = 10,
  dry_run = TRUE,
  .progress = FALSE
)
window_statistics
#> # slideimp table: 3 x 4
#>  start end window_n  subset_local
#>      1  50       50 <double [50]>
#>     41  90       50 <double [50]>
#>     81 100       20 <double [20]>

# Sliding-window K-NN imputation
imputed_knn <- slide_imp(
  beta_matrix,
  location = location,
  k = 5,
  window_size = 50,
  overlap_size = 10,
  min_window_n = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)
imputed_knn
#> Method: slide_imp (K-NN imputation)
#> Dimensions: 20 x 100
#> 
#>          feature1  feature2  feature3  feature4  feature5  feature6
#> sample1 0.3486482 0.7385414 0.4077444 0.1607935 0.3924661 0.2434143
#> sample2 0.5338935 0.4724364 0.9663621 0.4922511 0.5061132 0.3923603
#> sample3 0.7185848 0.7351035 0.6724479 0.3162537 0.7634236 1.0000000
#> sample4 0.1734418 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.0000000 0.2106358
#> sample5 0.4499620 0.5306182 0.5685354 0.5383513 0.4680080 0.8518388
#> sample6 0.3768380 0.5570723 0.8764909 0.5276245 0.6722794 0.5740639
#> # Showing 6 of 20 rows and 6 of 100 columns

# Sliding-window PCA imputation
imputed_pca <- slide_imp(
  beta_matrix,
  location = location,
  ncp = 2,
  window_size = 50,
  overlap_size = 10,
  min_window_n = 10,
  .progress = FALSE
)
imputed_pca

# K-NN imputation with flanking windows
imputed_flank <- slide_imp(
  beta_matrix,
  location = location,
  k = 2,
  window_size = 30,
  flank = TRUE,
  subset = c(10, 30, 70),
  min_window_n = 5,
  .progress = FALSE
)
imputed_flank
